g.text: The ambient model reproduces diurnal envelopes but not discrete events

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4f4e4a

g.text: Left: the deployed ambient model (`sensing/ambient.py`, history mode) run at the real day's timestamps

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4f4e4a

g.text: and shifted by one per-channel offset so its mean matches. Right: the same values against the 1:1 line —

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4f4e4a

g.text: temperature (r = 0.81) and illuminance (r = 0.84) follow it, CO₂ (r = 0.38) does not.

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #86847e

g.text: rather than from this background generator. n = 1 day, 1 room, 1 deployment; seeded (rng=0), single run.

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #86847e

g.text: — which is precisely why the closed loop takes its anomalies from explicit scenarios with a physics CO₂ model

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #86847e

g.text: diurnal model cannot know about the one occupancy event in the real day and places its own meeting spikes elsewhere

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #86847e

g.text: r and RMSE measure shape fidelity IN SAMPLE, not out-of-sample prediction. CO₂ is the deliberate miss: a generic

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #86847e

g.text: Source: real-trace-2026-07-10-london.csv + sensing/ambient.py (Table 6). The offset is fitted on this same day, so
